parole.significato: Any of various Jewish traditions that are not included in the Mishnah.
parole.testo: Aramaic baraita, an extraneous teaching. The word appears in the feminine (baraita rather than bara'ah), because it is actually short for matnita baraita, external Mishnah or teaching (and matnita is feminine).

parole.significato: A lively and fast-paced dance; (by extension) any quick and uneven movement.
parole.testo: * English surname of Aramaic origin, from בַּר נְבִיָּא (bar nəḇiyyā, literally “prophet’s son”). * Also as an English surname, from Old English Beornwald, from beorn (“young warrior”) + wealdan (“rule”) + Old Norse býr (“farmstead”).

parole.significato: Any location whose waters are supposed to have curative properties.
parole.testo: From Aramaic בֵּית חַסְדָּא (bēṯ ḥasdā, “House of Grace”).
